title: Invariant affine filtration for a split torus action
statement:
Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], let $r\geq0$, and let $T\simeq\mathbf G_{m,F}^r$ be a split torus [def-sc-group-scheme], where $\mathbf G_m(B)=B^\times$ for every commutative $F$-algebra $B$. Let $T$ act on a separated finite-type $F$-scheme $Y$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $V\subseteq Y$ be an invariant open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion]; invariant means that the action restricts to $T\times_FV\to V$. The scheme $V$ is separated and of finite type over $F$. Its reduction $V_{\mathrm{red}}$ is the reduced closed subscheme [def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion] defined by the sheaf of nilpotent sections of $\mathcal O_V$; it has the same underlying space as $V$. There exist an action on $V_{\mathrm{red}}$ making its inclusion into $V$ equivariant, an integer $N\geq0$, and a finite descending chain of invariant reduced closed subschemes
$$V_{\mathrm{red}}=Z_0\supseteq Z_1\supseteq\cdots\supseteq Z_N=\varnothing$$
such that every open complement $S_j=Z_j\setminus Z_{j+1}$, for $0\leq j<N$, is affine [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Every $Z_j$ and $S_j$ is separated and of finite type over $F$, and all inclusions are equivariant for the induced actions. The empty $V$ case permits $N=0$. No normality, smoothness, projectivity, effective-action hypothesis, or restriction on the characteristic is imposed.

source.place: Agent-formulated geometric supporting input for the concentration prerequisite to Section 22d, Theorem 22.50, printed p.480; not stated or proved in Milne. WANTED: H. Sumihiro, Equivariant completion, J. Math. Kyoto Univ. 14 (1974), 1--28, Corollary 2 (invariant affine neighborhoods on normal torus varieties), followed by reduction and Noetherian induction. The full arbitrary-scheme filtration is the agent-formulated statement. No Stacks tag is asserted for this equivariant result.

proof.text: A field is Noetherian, since each ideal is zero or the whole field. Hence $Y$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. The open immersion $V\to Y$ is quasi-compact by [lem-sfb-noetherian-open-immersion-qc], therefore finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-qc-open-immersion-finite-type]. Composition [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change] makes $V$ finite type over $F$. Its diagonal is the pullback of the closed diagonal of $Y$ to $V\times_FV$, so [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change] proves separatedness. The locally closed stratum theorem [lem-dl-a1-locally-closed-stratum-separated-finite-type], applied in $Y$ to the subset $|V|$ and open $V$, makes $X=V_{\mathrm{red}}$ separated and finite type. Its reduced induced structure agrees with the reduction by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme].

source.place: Tags 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian), 01T3 (lemma-composition-finite-type); properties.tex Tag 01OX; schemes.tex Tags 01J3 and 01JY.

proof.text: Put $i:X\hookrightarrow V$. Use [lem-trf-split-lattice-torus-projection] with $L=\mathbf Z^r$: $T\times_FX$ is reduced. Thus the composite $T\times_FX\to T\times_FV\to V$ factors through $i$ by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-source-factors-through-closed-subscheme]. This supplies $a_X:T\times_FX\to X$. The identity and associativity laws hold after composition with $i$, by the laws on $V$. They therefore hold on $X$: a closed immersion cancels on morphisms, since on affine charts its ring maps are surjective and maps out of a quotient are determined by their composites. The same cancellation proves equivariance of $i$. This argument uses the whole algebraic action, including nonreduced test algebras, rather than just its $F$-points.

source.place: Tag 0356 (lemma-map-into-reduction); torus reduced-product input as in the cited split-lattice projection node.

proof.text: The scheme $X$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal], every nonempty family of closed subsets of $|X|$ has an inclusion-minimal member. We prove by this well-founded induction that every invariant reduced closed subscheme $C\subseteq X$ has the required finite filtration, where the action on $C$ and its equivariant inclusion are included in the induction's data. The empty $C$ has the length-zero filtration. For a nonempty $C$, assume the assertion for every invariant reduced closed subscheme with strictly smaller support. The stratum theorem [lem-dl-a1-locally-closed-stratum-separated-finite-type], applied to $|C|\subseteq |Y|$, makes $C$ separated and finite type over $F$. Thus the following steps may be carried out for this $C$.

source.place: Tag 01OZ (lemma-Noetherian-topology); agent Noetherian induction with empty base case.

proof.text: The field $F$ is perfect: in characteristic $p>0$, every $b\in F$ has a root of $z^p-b$; in characteristic zero every field is perfect. Since $C$ is reduced and finite type, [lem-kun-geometric-reduced-perfect] gives geometric reducedness and finite presentation over $F$. Let $W$ be its smooth locus. By [lem-pur-geometrically-reduced-dense-smooth-open], $W$ is the union of its smooth open subschemes and is dense in $C$. It is nonempty because $C$ is nonempty. Source locality [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-local-on-source] makes $W\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ smooth. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular] it is regular, and by [rem-pc-regular-normal](1) it is normal. As a reduced locally closed subscheme of $Y$, it is also separated and finite type by [lem-dl-a1-locally-closed-stratum-separated-finite-type].

source.place: Tags 056V (lemma-geometrically-reduced-dense-smooth-open), 0B8X (lemma-dense-smooth-open-variety-over-perfect-field), 056S (lemma-smooth-regular); agent assembly of their cited statements.

proof.text: Write $a:T\times_F C\to C$, $p:T\times_F C\to C$, and $q:T\times_F C\to T$ for the action and the two projections. The structural morphism $T\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ is smooth by [lem-trf-split-lattice-torus-projection], hence flat by [lem-pc-smooth-flat]. The structure map of $C$ is finitely presented by step 4. Applying [lem-sfb-scheme-lfp-smooth-flat-base-change] to it shows that the smooth locus of $q$ is precisely $p^{-1}W$. The shear $\theta(t,c)=(t,a(t,c))$ is an isomorphism over $T$, with inverse $(t,c)\mapsto(t,a(t^{-1},c))$; the group identities verify both composites. Smoothness on an open is unchanged by an isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes](c). Since $q\theta=q$, its smooth locus is $\theta^{-1}(p^{-1}W)$. Therefore $a^{-1}W=p^{-1}W$. In particular the action on $T\times_FW$ factors through $W$ by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme]. Its laws follow by composing with the open inclusion and cancelling it using [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-monomorphism]. Thus $W$ is an invariant normal open, with scheme-theoretic action.

source.place: Tag 02V4 (lemma-set-points-where-fibres-smooth), case (2); agent shear-isomorphism argument; Tag 01V6 (lemma-smooth-characterize) and schemes open factorization.

proof.text: Choose $w\in W$. Apply [lem-sfb-sumihiro-normal-torus-affine-neighbourhood] to the normal separated finite-type $F$-scheme $W$ with its restricted $T$-action. It gives an invariant affine open $A\subseteq W$ containing $w$. Then $A$ is also an open of $C$, nonempty, and its inclusion into $C$ is equivariant. The shear of step 5 restricts to an automorphism of $T\times_FA$: the action and the action by inverse both restrict to $A$. Consequently, as open subsets of $T\times_FC$, $a^{-1}A=p^{-1}A$. Taking complements gives $a^{-1}(|C|\setminus A)=p^{-1}(|C|\setminus A)$.

source.place: Agent concentration prerequisite; WANTED: Sumihiro, Equivariant completion (1974), Corollary 2. Milne Theorem 22.50, p.480, motivates the prerequisite but does not prove it.

proof.text: Let $D\hookrightarrow C$ be the reduced induced closed subscheme with support $|C|\setminus A$, supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. The source $T\times_FD$ is reduced by [lem-trf-split-lattice-torus-projection]. Its map to $C$ under the action has image in $|D|$: $T\times_FD$ is the pullback of the closed immersion $D\to C$ along $p$, so its map to $T\times_FC$ is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change], with underlying image $p^{-1}|D|$. Indeed the image lies in $p^{-1}|D|$ since the square commutes; conversely, for $z\in T\times_FC$ with $p(z)=c\in|D|$, let $e\in D$ be the point over $c$; [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-points] gives points over $(z,e)$ in bijection with $\operatorname{Spec}(\kappa(z)\otimes_{\kappa(c)}\kappa(e))$, which is nonempty because a tensor product of two field extensions of $\kappa(c)$ is a nonzero ring. The complement equality in step 6 then puts that image in $a^{-1}|D|$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-source-factors-through-closed-subscheme] to factor the action through $D$. The group identities follow by cancelling its closed immersion, exactly as in step 2. The composite $D\to X$ is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-products]; hence $D$ is an invariant reduced closed subscheme of $X$. Its support is strictly smaller than that of $C$, since $A$ is nonempty.

source.place: Tags 01J3 (lemma-reduced-closed-subscheme), 0356 (lemma-map-into-reduction), 01JT (lemma-points-fibre-product); morphisms.tex Tag 01QR for the base-changed closed immersion. Agent complement argument.

proof.text: Apply the induction hypothesis to $D$, obtaining $D=D_0\supseteq\cdots\supseteq D_m=\varnothing$. Prepend $C$ to this chain. The new first difference is exactly the open subscheme $A$, since $D$ was defined by its reduced closed complement; all later differences are those of the chain on $D$. The new first difference is affine by step 6, and all later ones are affine by induction. Closed inclusions compose by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-products]. Each member and difference is a reduced locally closed subscheme of $Y$, so [lem-dl-a1-locally-closed-stratum-separated-finite-type] gives separatedness and finite type over $F$ for each. Every inclusion is equivariant: the new ones are restrictions of the action constructed in step 7 and the given action on $A$, and the remaining ones are equivariant by induction. This proves the induction step. Taking $C=X$ gives the desired chain on $V_{\mathrm{red}}$, with $N=m+1$ in the nonempty step and $N=0$ for empty $V$.
